## Summary

Adds a new unit suite for the public launch barrel of the Electrobun desktop platform: `packages/app-core/platforms/electrobun/src/launch/index.test.ts` (+789/-0, new file only — no production code, no existing tests modified or deleted).

The barrel (`src/launch/index.ts`) is what `rpc-handlers.ts` imports (`import { LaunchOrchestrator } from "./launch"`), so the suite drives every behavior through that exact consumer boundary instead of deep module paths. It covers branches none of the three sibling suites touch:

- **LaunchStore** (via barrel): deterministic empty snapshot on an injected clock (including the unknown-database snapshot and its recovery actions), defensive clones out of `getSnapshot()` and `update()`, verbatim `initialSnapshot` installation, explicit update events vs. automatic `launch.phase.changed` events on phase change only, monotonic sequences with payload cloning, newest-wins retention under `maxEvents`, tail-window clamping (`limit <= 0` clamps to 1) with strict `sequence > afterSequence` filtering, and both `reset(snapshot)` / `reset()` forms.
- **LaunchOrchestrator classification** (via barrel): every agent-state branch (`error`, `not_started`, `stopped`, `starting` with and without port), `agent-api-ready` while boot is still progressing, `auth-checking` / `first-run-checking` holds when endpoints return nothing, `bootstrapRequired` escalation, required-gate precedence (pairing > bootstrap > cloud-provisioned first-run > local runtime), port-null short-circuit (gate readers never called), port `0` passed through to readers and `apiBase`, boot-reader failure falling back to diagnostics without rejecting, non-`Error` reader rejections stringified without faking a "checking" phase, live agent error taking precedence over diagnostics `lastError`, all five blocking database statuses forcing `error` with database-recovery guidance overriding gate suggestions, and per-phase suggested actions.
- **LaunchOrchestrator commands** (via barrel): `tailEvents` forwarding to an injected store, retry semantics for `not_started` / `running` / `error` agents with the request event recorded before dispatch, rejection when either dynamic-view host is absent, manifest registration with `{ update: true }` proven by opening twice, serialized snapshot + event tail delivered into the opened session plus the `launch.diagnostics.opened` store event, and synchronous bug-report bundle creation with the exact markdown/json payloads and the `launch.bug_report.created` event.

All fixtures are injected through constructor options (clocks, readers, adapters); the only mocks are spies on those injected collaborators. No `vi.mock`, no `vi.hoisted`, no type-level assertions.

## What is covered

Every exported runtime symbol of `packages/ui/src/services/local-inference/recommendation.ts`:

- **`classifyRecommendationPlatform`** — android/ios (top-level and `hardware.mobile` precedence over the OS platform), apple-silicon even with a GPU present, linux-gpu/linux-cpu split, desktop-gpu/desktop-cpu fallback.
- **`catalogDownloadSizeGb` / `catalogDownloadSizeBytes`** — size comes from the model record itself regardless of catalog argument; GiB-to-bytes rounding.
- **`assessCatalogModelFit`** — mobile RAM floor plus the 80% wontfit / 65% tight thresholds; desktop CPU-only half-RAM effective memory; Apple Silicon full-RAM; discrete-GPU VRAM preference — each across fits/tight/wontfit bands.
- **`selectRecommendedModelForSlot`** — ladder walk largest-first for TEXT_LARGE and smallest-first for TEXT_SMALL, skipping unfitting rungs; the long-context bump reordering TEXT_LARGE on hosts with >= 16 GB RAM or VRAM headroom (and NOT applying below the threshold or on TEXT_SMALL); empty-result shape (`model: null`, `fit: null`, exact reason string); mobile degradation past the 4B ladder floor to a fitting 2B fallback candidate; fallback ordering by slot direction; hidden and non-default-eligible models excluded from fallbacks; kernel gating via `binaryKernels` (required-kernel filtering, trust-the-catalog when no probe exists, unsupported-backend-only drop, satisfied-anchor coexisting with an advertised unsupported backend).
- **`selectRecommendedModels`** — both slots returned with echoed labels and one shared platform classification.
- **`recommendForFirstRun`** — the full resolution order against synthetic catalogs plus the real `MODEL_CATALOG`: preferred published tier, first published eligible fallback, pending-preferred skip, consultation of the shared tier publish-status hint map, last-resort to preferred-then-any eligible tier when everything is pending, hidden-entry skip, and `null` only with no default-eligible entry.
- **`chooseSmallerFallbackModel`** — strictly-smaller descent of the slot ladder (equal-sized tiers skipped), unknown current id treated as unbounded, fit-gate skipping, out-of-ladder mobile fallback, `null` when nothing smaller fits, TEXT_LARGE default and slot-parameter routing.

## What

Adds `packages/evidence/src/queue/index.test.ts`: a new unit suite for the GPU vision job queue's public barrel (`packages/evidence/src/queue/index.ts`), which previously had no same-named test file anywhere in the repo. The diff is one new file, +744/-0 — no production code changes.

## Why

The barrel declares the public surface of the queue module (#14543). Every sibling module had its own suite; the surface consumers actually import from was untested. This PR covers that boundary behaviorally.

## How it is tested

All runtime symbols are imported from `./index.ts` and driven for real — no module mocks:

- `parseJob`: valid round-trip incl. params; non-JSON -> typed `QueueJobInvalidError` (`QUEUE_JOB_INVALID`, issues preserved); empty-string field; array params; every missing field listed at once.
- `makeJobId` + `claimOrder`: timestamp-prefix FIFO ordering, same-ms tie determinism, non-job filtering + sort.
- `decideEnqueue`: accept below cap; refuse at/above cap with exact reason.
- Connectivity latch: healthy start; first-failure stamp without drain; drain exactly at window boundary and latching; full reset via `onServiceOk`.
- `isConnectivityFailure` across all four statuses; `drainSkipResult` honest-skip shape (no fabricated data).
- Typed errors: `QueueBackpressureError` name/code/message/context.
- `FileJobQueue` over real tmp directories: creates all four `QUEUE_DIRS`; enqueue -> oldest-first claim -> complete -> `readResult`; backpressure throw at cap; null result probe.
- `mergeAnalyzerResult` on real fs: fresh schema-1 doc creation; second analyzer preserves the first (no lost update).
- `processJob`: unknown-analyzer failure; completed contact merging data and clearing a latch; transient connectivity requeue leaving the job pending with no record; drained honest skip recording reason only.
- `runQueueWorker` with `stopWhenIdle`: drains to idle with correct per-action counts and claimed/processed/idle event sequence.
- `QueueExecutor`: cpu-tier delegation runs inline unchanged; gpu-tier with no worker produces the deterministic honest skip naming the missing worker while the job stays enqueued.
- `runQueueCli` over captured io: usage exit 0; structured `CLI_USAGE` error line + exit 1; enqueue writes one pending job and reports its id.

## Summary

Adds a new unit suite `packages/core/src/features/advanced-capabilities/experience/service.test.ts` covering the previously untested surface of `ExperienceService` (`packages/core/src/features/advanced-capabilities/experience/service.ts`). This is a **test-only change**: no production file is modified, the diff is a single new file (+N/-0), and behavior is unchanged.

The two existing suites next to the module stay untouched: `service.persistence.test.ts` (hydration/embedding-failure/persistence boundaries) and `service.findSimilar.test.ts` (fail-open semantic search). This suite covers the remaining public surface by driving the real service over the in-memory mock runtime from `@elizaos/core/testing` — no module mocks, no live model, no real DB:

- **recordExperience**: default type/outcome/confidence/importance, tag normalization (lowercase/trim/dedupe; `[domain, type]` fallback), keyword derivation and frequency ranking, explicit-keyword case preservation, associated-entity dedupe, single TEXT_EMBEDDING call wiring with the concatenated context/action/result/learning text, and contradiction cross-linking into `getExperienceGraph` (stored `contradicts` plus the inferred `supports` link it provably co-produces).
- **Reads/hydration**: defensive clones from `getExperience` (caller mutations cannot corrupt store state), `null` for missing ids, and tag/keyword backfill for stored records persisted without them.
- **updateExperience**: `null` on missing id; metadata-only updates keep the stored embedding and skip the model entirely; content updates regenerate embedding + keywords while `id`/`agentId`/`createdAt` stay pinned against override attempts.
- **deleteExperience**: durable delete removes record and index entries, returns `true`, then `false` on repeat.
- **Listing/queries**: quality-descending order (confidence × importance inside the decay grace window) with limit enforcement, per-field filters (type/outcome/domain/tags/minImportance/timeRange including open-ended ranges), access-count tracking on `queryExperiences` but not `listExperiences`, and `includeRelated` appending referenced-but-unselected records.
- **dedupeDuplicateExperiences**: empty-store and distinct-learning no-ops; merge semantics (max confidence/importance, summed accessCount, latest lastAccessedAt, unioned tags/keywords/entities); supersede-with-clamp path (survivor confidence clamped to 0.4, `supersedes` pointer set); hard-delete path removing the duplicate durably.
- **analyzeExperiences**: zeroed empty-store analysis, frequency/pattern/reliability computation with the top reliability tier recommendations, and alternative extraction from correction beliefs and "instead" clauses.
- **stop()**: final persistence of every in-memory experience.

Every assertion records observed behavior of the current implementation (e.g., keyword frequency ordering includes the defaulted type-tag term; same-action pairs produce both a stored `contradicts` link and an inferred `supports` link because the shared action/domain vocabulary yields four common keywords).

## What this adds

A new vitest suite for `packages/core/src/features/advanced-capabilities/actions/room.ts` — the unified ROOM_OP action (`roomOpAction`) and its four child actions. The module previously had no suite at its own path; the adjacent `room.mute.test.ts` covers the timed-mute persistence and `scope=server` success slices, and this PR deliberately leaves that file untouched.

The new cases drive the real handler/validate through a deterministic map-backed runtime (only the model boundary is scripted) and cover branches nothing else exercised:

- **Op resolution** — `ROOM_OP_REQUIRED` when nothing resolves; the `restore_chat` alias; whitespace/case normalization of `action`; keyword inference from message text via the real i18n term data (`"follow this room"`).
- **durationMinutes parsing** — integer strings accepted and normalized (`"30"` → timed mute with `scheduleAutoUnmuteIso` + persisted `agentMuteUntilIso`); zero/negative rejected as `ROOM_DURATION_INVALID` (the falsy-zero encodes an untimed mute, so these must not slip through).
- **scope=server failure branches** — room without `worldId` → `ROOM_SERVER_NOT_FOUND`; missing world record → `ROOM_SERVER_NOT_FOUND`; unmute of an inactive server → `ROOM_UNMUTE_PRECONDITION_FAILED`; `GUILD` alias honored case-insensitively; platform+chatName resolution muting the correct world while siblings stay untouched.
- **Connector-targeted ops** — follow matched by case-insensitive partial chatName; `ROOM_NOT_FOUND` naming the platform; unfollow precondition failure carrying `currentState`; timed connector mute announcing `Muted <name> on <platform> for N minutes.` with expiry persisted on room metadata.
- **Current-room model gate** — decline leaves participant state untouched; unclear model answers default to decline (observed behavior); missing state → `STATE_REQUIRED`; mute-while-MUTED fails the precondition *before* any model call (asserted); approval with a missing room record → `ROOM_NOT_FOUND` after the decision memory was written (ordering pinned by assertion).
- **Child actions** — forced-op validate matrix for MUTE_ROOM / UNMUTE_ROOM / FOLLOW_ROOM / UNFOLLOW_ROOM across MUTED/FOLLOWED/NONE states; end-to-end forced mute with no parameters; validate refusing runtimes without participant-state access; vacuous availability when no op requested; connector-unresolvable and server-scope-follow rejections.

No mocks asserting their own return values: every assertion reads the stores the inbound mute gate consults (`participant` state map, room/world metadata) or the returned ActionResult.

## What

Adds `packages/agent/src/services/pendant-session/index.test.ts` and nothing else (+698/-0, one new file). No production file is touched.

The module had no same-named suite anywhere on `develop`; the neighbouring `repository.test.ts` covers `repository.ts` internals and is left exactly as-is.

## What the new suite covers (20 cases)

- **Barrel wiring:** runtime re-exports of `createPendantSessionRepository`, both repository classes, and `pendantSessionSchema` are identity-equal to the deep modules, and the schema object exposes exactly the three tables (`getTableConfig` names asserted).
- **Factory:** `createPendantSessionRepository` builds a working `SqlPendantSessionRepository` (proven by real `create` true/false behaviour through a driver double), and fails closed on every method when the runtime database adapter or its transaction hook is missing.
- **SQL load normalization:** raw snake_case rows in both array and `{ rows }` result shapes normalize into one document — numeric strings parsed, JSON word/segment-id arrays decoded, non-object entries ignored, lease present only when all three lease columns exist.
- **Failure paths:** non-array `words_json` rejects instead of coercing; unknown driver-provided session states reject through the contract enum; a vanished row during revision update reports "row disappeared"; a revision-0 update refuses before touching the database.
- **Delete ordering:** insight refs, then segments, then the session row, each scoped by owner/agent/session.
- **Escaping:** single quotes inside scope values become doubled quoted literals, never raw interpolation.
- **In-memory repository:** scope-exact loads, duplicate-create keeps the first snapshot, returned documents are detached clones (deep mutations never reach the store), latest-active selection across scopes with deterministic tie handling, session updates that preserve stored segments/insight refs (and create empty children for unknown keys), whole-list insight-ref replacement including clearing, segment replacement-in-place without duplication, and idempotent deletes.

## Observed-behaviour note

`InMemoryPendantSessionRepository.loadLatest` breaks equal `startedAt` ties by keeping the lexically lower session id first, while the SQL path orders `started_at DESC, id DESC`. The test records what the code does today; if that divergence is unwanted it is a production change for a separate, justified pull request — not something this diff alters.

The hook owns non-trivial client-side behaviour worth pinning: queue ordering with a never-scheduled-last sentinel, loud-vs-silent reload semantics, upsert/prune merges across CRUD, and error surfacing including fallbacks for non-`Error` rejections.

## Coverage

- **Ordering** — ascending by `nextRunAtMs`; triggers without a schedule sort last; ties break by `displayName`; sorting writes into a copy so the server-supplied array is left untouched; empty queue loads successfully.
- **load semantics** — loud loads toggle `triggersLoading` true→false and drop a stale list on failure; silent loads never raise the flag and retain previously loaded triggers; `ensureTriggersLoaded` routes loudly before the first load and silently afterwards.
- **Run history** — `loadTriggerRuns` stores history per trigger id without clobbering other entries; failures surface `Error.message` verbatim or the operation-specific fallback for non-`Error` rejections.
- **CRUD merges** — `createTrigger` inserts in sorted position and replaces any stale entry carrying the same id instead of duplicating it; `updateTrigger` swaps the record in place and re-sorts; `deleteTrigger` removes only its own run-history entry.
- **runTriggerNow** — replaces an existing entry or appends an unknown one from the run response; refetches the whole list when the response omits the trigger; returns the response's `ok` and records failures.
- **Flags & errors** — every mutation toggles `triggersSaving`, clears `triggerError` on success, sets the observed message on failure; health refresh fires after successful mutations.

The suite drives the real hook through `renderHook` (`@testing-library/react`) against a controlled `../api` transport double — the established pattern of sibling tests in `src/state/`. Assertions cover observable state transitions of the real module; no mock echoes its own stub.

## Evidence

Validated locally on current `origin/develop@d77eb55bc0` and re-run inside the pushed head `7413818e9611d53b3cea7ab413ed6c4a5e1321e5`:

- `bunx vitest run src/state/useTriggersState.test.ts` → **Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 24 passed (24)**
- `bunx biome check packages/ui/src/state/useTriggersState.test.ts` → **Checked 1 file, no fixes applied** (clean)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/ui` → **zero diagnostics mention the new test file** (pre-existing unrelated package errors unchanged)

As a fork contribution, hosted CI does not run on this pull request; the counts above are the validation record.

None — additive test coverage only; no runtime behaviour is modified.

## What

Adds a new unit suite for the fog voice-orb concept (`packages/ui/stories/src/concepts/fog.ts`), placed with the package's collected tests at `packages/ui/src/__tests__/stories-concepts-fog.test.ts`. Test-only: no production source, config, or export changes — exactly one new file, +636/−0.

## Why

`fog.ts` had no same-named test anywhere on develop. The concept is consumed through `stories/src/concepts/index.ts`, which registers it in the CONCEPTS list the voice-orb gallery iterates, so every shell/mote behaviour the gallery relies on was unverified. The suite drives the real module through the same injected three/webgpu module surface the orb-kit harness hands every concept builder, and every expectation is recomputed independently — no mocked return value is asserted against itself.

## Coverage (21 cases)

- Descriptor contract: id/label `fog`, family `mood`, callable builder.
- Scene structure: ten sphere shells (24×16 segments, radii strictly descending within [0.7, 1.25]) followed by one 80-mote Points cloud with `frustumCulled = false`.
- Material contract: translucent, `depthWrite = false`, NormalBlending; slate-blue channel ordering (b > g > r) on every shell and on the mote cloud; build-time opacities 0.4 (motes) and [0.1, 0.15] (shells); mote size 0.022; initial mote radii within [0.5, 1.25].
- Frame animation: exact rest at t=0 (all rotations zero, unity scale); breathe scale `1 + energy·0.06` applied as a uniform scalar; respond colour lift of +0.05/+0.06/+0.08 per channel and opacity lift +0.015 held under the 0.24 ceiling; listen dim −0.008 stacking subtractively with respond via the same `min(0.24, …)` formula; each shell spins at a constant signed rate about exactly one axis (population {x:3, y:5, z:2}) with directions alternating across the stack while non-spinning components stay inside their ≤0.08 wobble bounds; shell centres wander on bounded ±0.025 sinusoidal drift on all three axes; every frame rewrites all 80 mote positions inside r ∈ [0.42, 1.33], actually moves them between distant frames, and flags the position attribute `needsUpdate`; mote opacity resets from the build-time 0.4 to the animated 0.34 floor (`0.34 + respond·0.12`).
- Input contract: the `low` band is provably unread (identical whole-state snapshot with low 0 vs 1); replaying any frame reproduces byte-identical world state (stateless per-frame math).
- Teardown: dispose releases all 11 geometries and all 11 materials and detaches everything the builder added.

## Summary

Adds a colocated unit suite for `packages/core/src/features/advanced-capabilities/personality/services/character-file-manager.ts`, which had no same-named test file anywhere in the repository on current `origin/develop`.

The suite drives the real service class end to end against a temporary filesystem harness (`ELIZA_STATE_DIR` redirect plus per-test cwd): file discovery (malformed and wrong-name candidates skipped before a match), modification validation (schema short-circuit, safety rules, exact capacity boundaries at 20 bio / 50 topics and their overflows), additive merge application with durable rewrite of the detected character file on disk, backup retention capped at ten newest JSON files, newest-first backup listing with filename-timestamp parsing and mtime fallback, typed `CHARACTER_BACKUP_FAILED` wrap when the source vanishes, modification-history projection (metadata precedence, detected-path fallback, default limit), and restoration gates including persistence-failure atomicity and the strict one-minute backup-match window.

## Relation to #26297

This supersedes the author's closed #26297 for the same module. That suite was closed because it asserted behaviors flagged in review: acceptance of non-canonical names and duplicate/case-duplicate accumulation in collections. This suite deliberately asserts none of those behaviors — collection cases only exercise distinct appends and exact-duplicate-of-existing skipping — and adds coverage for branches the prior suite missed: the apply-time and restore-time character-file writes, history filePath fallback to the detected file, restoreFromHistory missing-filePath / missing-timestamp rejections, and the persistence-success commit path. A production normalization/deduplication fix with stable-order regression coverage remains open follow-up work, as requested in the #26297 review.

- `ensureCompatApiAuthorized` trust matrix over hand-built Node req/res objects (loopback OWNER, remote tokenless 401, configured `ELIZA_API_TOKEN` accept/reject)
- `isDevEnvironment` NODE_ENV spellings

## What

Extends the unit suite for `packages/agent/src/runtime/sandbox-character.ts` with 28 new cases (+552/-0, append-only; no existing case or line is modified). This is a test-only change with no production behaviour change.

## Why

The existing suite covered the main merge path but left several exported branches unpinned: `sandboxOwnsConnectors` had no direct tests at all, the id/name precedence chains were only partially exercised, and several local-file, connector-merge, and credential-strip branches had no coverage.

## What is now covered

- `sandboxOwnsConnectors`: true only when the variable trims to exactly `"1"` (`" 1 "` true; `"0"`, `"true"`, `""`, absent false).
- `resolveSandboxRouteAgentId`: whitespace trimming; whitespace-only treated as absent.
- Name precedence: parsed name → `ELIZA_AGENT_NAME` → `AGENT_NAME`; blank parsed name falls through.
- Id precedence chain: route id → embedded character id (non-string ids skipped) → `SANDBOX_AGENT_ID` → lowercased hyphenated name slug.
- Field mapping: username/system/style/settings/messageExamples passthrough; scalar bio/topics/adjectives/postExamples normalize to single-element arrays; non-string array members filtered; blank scalars omit the field; an explicitly empty array is preserved verbatim.
- Knowledge + lore ordered concatenation through the public entry point.
- Local-file seam: absolute `ELIZA_CHARACTER_PATH` honored verbatim; injected JSON wins over any local file; `ELIZA_DISABLE_LOCAL_CHARACTER=1` skips discovery but not injected JSON; unreadable file warns and boots default; empty file treated as absent without warning.
- JSON bodies that are `null` or primitives leave the config unchanged; missing-name overrides warn and keep config unchanged.
- Default-agent merge: the existing default entry moves to index 0, override fields win, unrelated fields survive, secondary entries shift.
- Connector application under `ELIZA_SANDBOX_OWNS_CONNECTORS=1`: merge over pre-existing connectors, rejection of array- and scalar-valued connector config, info log naming owned keys.
- `applySandboxConnectorOwnership`: provisioned flag must be exactly `"1"` (untrimmed ignored); empty-string tokens retained (truthiness); nested stripping across `connectors`, legacy `channels`, `config.env`, `config.env.vars`, and per-agent `settings`/`settings.extra`/`settings.secrets` while unrelated keys survive; no summary log when nothing was stripped; missing config tolerated.
- `prepareSandboxRuntimeConfig` sequencing: identity applied before projection (projection observes the injected character), ownership strips projected gateway-owned credentials last, container-owned connectors survive the whole pipeline, returns null without a route id while still applying identity.
- `applySandboxIdentityFromEnv` applies identity and returns null when no route id exists.

All expectations record observed behaviour of the module as it stands on develop; assertions drive the real module through its injected env/file seams (the logger is module-mocked exactly as in the pre-existing cases).

- Start outcomes: `accepted` (uuid id, pending status, empty phase log, tier persisted), `deduped` on a known idempotency key, `rejected-busy` carrying the active op id; idempotency gate checked before the busy gate.
- Classification: custom classifier tiers recorded; conservative `cold` default when none is wired; classify context snapshotted BEFORE `prepare()` runs — proven by mutating provider state inside prepare and asserting the classifier still sees pre-prepare values while a subsequent start sees the mutation.
- `prepare()` contract: returned intent replaces the request intent for both classification and execution; `undefined` keeps the original.
- Async lifecycle to success: validate → strategy-applied phases → health-check, with the strategy receiving the live runtime + prepared intent, its returned runtime passed to `runForRuntime`, phase details carrying passed/failed counts and monotone timestamps.
- Failure branches: `no-strategy-for-tier` (and its precedence over the runtime lookup), `no-runtime`, plain throw → `strategy-failed`, thrown `code: "vault-resolve-failed"` preserved, failed health check flipping only the last phase to `failed` while earlier phases stay immutable.
- Single-flight: concurrent submissions serialize; the second is rejected busy against the in-flight op id, then the first completes to succeeded.
- Query delegation: `get`/`list`/`findActive` passthrough.

Coverage driven through the public path:

- Native navigate-view queue: apply→resolve(`true`), durable consumption (no redelivery), strict FIFO across pending intents, explicit-`false` retry semantics (decliner sees initial delivery + replay), throwing-listener isolation, the 16-item overflow bound resolving the dropped intent `false`, and legacy non-queued passthrough.

b0:T11a4,## Summary

Follow-up to #25642. The independent CHANGES_REQUESTED review by @andreolf on that PR (merged before resolution) reported four safety gaps in `wellFormedUnicodeSchemaStructure` / `walkSchemaMapEntry` / `assertSchemaAnnotationsSerializable` plus two additional blocking findings by @lalalune on this PR's head `b063660`. All six are addressed at the amended head `4343f5979dc4`.

## Changes

### 1. `__proto__` setter mutation (object + map entry rebuild)
Rebuilt projected nodes on a null prototype and restore the source prototype after all keys are defined. `defineProperty` with first-write-wins collision policy — same policy as `walkDeep` (#18081).

### 2. Sparse array free-ride
Array length now charged up-front in the generic-array branch; dense arrays that were thrown at ~70k elements now pass up to the visit budget.

### 3. Accessor in properties map silently survived
`walkSchemaMapEntry` now fails closed on accessor descriptors (same as object branch).

### 4. Numeric accessor in array silently skipped
Generic-array branch now fails closed on any accessor descriptor.

### 5. Wire assert over-charged schema region (defeated walker authority)
Every container (tool wrapper, properties map) was charged, capping effective depth at ~31 vs declared 64.

### 6. Keyword-edge exemption spoofable (NEW — lalalune)
Any object named `"properties"` or `"items"` was treated as a free edge; hostile wrappers could nest same-named keys to avoid depth charging entirely (unbounded work / stack overflow before dispatch).

**The fix eliminates all name-based exemptions.** Every edge now charges uniformly +1 depth; every node charges +1 visit. The doubled budget (`2×MAX_WELL_FORMED_DEPTH + 8 = 136`) guarantees a schema at the walker's full authority still passes, while any hostile deep/wide structure is bounded. ToolSet lazy SDK accessors are never observed because the check traverses the wrapper region (charging visits/depth) but only enforces accessor rejection + cycle guard + visit budget inside annotation subtrees — exactly as the function name and doc comment always claimed.

| Plugin tests (targeted Cerebras/Cerebras-native-tools) | **78/78** pass |

b1:T2e61,
Adds unit coverage for `useShellControllerSync` (`packages/ui/src/components/shell/shell-controller-sync/useShellControllerSync.ts`).

When this work started, current `origin/develop` already carried a three-case suite for the hook, so this change is strictly additive: it appends cases to the existing suite and removes nothing. The new cases drive the real hook through an injected in-memory authority transport and assert observable behavior for branches the suite did not yet reach:

- stale-authority filtering: states that regress generation or snapshot sequence are ignored; a newer sequence on the same generation is applied
- endpoint identity changes are reported as errors and the prior state is kept
- an invalid follower snapshot from the authority disconnects the follower and reports the rejection instead of adopting it
- connection failure moves the follower from `connecting` to `disconnected` and reports the transport error
- pings apply refreshed authority state delivered by `heartbeat`, and heartbeat failures are reported
- owner command completion: unmounted handler completes `{ ok: false }` with "owner controller is not mounted"; handler rejections complete with the thrown reason (both `Error` and non-`Error`); an authority that rejects a successful completion surfaces "authority rejected command completion"
- command requests from another generation or while not owner are ignored entirely
- dispatch routing: lone owners dispatch locally to their own handler (endpoint `local`) and refuse without one; followers forward through `dispatchCommand` and surface its failure strings, including the default "owner command failed"
- snapshot publishing is owner-only and reports publish failures; targeted delivery is owner-only with an authority transport and reports rejection

Evidence (all quoted from real runs against current `origin/develop`, base `e3e63588fd59`):

- `bunx vitest run src/components/shell/shell-controller-sync/__tests__/useShellControllerSync.test.tsx` in `packages/ui`: **1 file passed, 18 tests passed (18)** — 3 pre-existing plus 15 new; zero failures
- `bunx biome check --write <file>`: clean ("Checked 1 file... No fixes applied"), with `biome.json` present at the repo root and sparse-checkout disabled
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in `packages/ui`: the new test file appears nowhere in the output
- The diff touches only `packages/ui/src/components/shell/shell-controller-sync/__tests__/useShellControllerSync.test.tsx`: +586/-0, no production behavior changed

Note: this is a fork contribution, so hosted CI does not run on this pull request; the counts above are the verification record.

## What this PR does

Adds a new unit suite for the `lava` voice-orb concept (`packages/ui/stories/src/concepts/lava.ts`), which had no same-named test file anywhere on develop. The diff is a single new test file: `packages/ui/src/__tests__/stories-concepts-lava.test.ts` (+573/-0). No production code is touched.

## How it is tested

The suite drives the real module through the seam orb-kit designs for exactly this purpose: concepts receive an injected `THREE` module surface (`WebGPUModule = Record<string, any>`), so the tests hand lava a recording double and assert lava's own computed behaviour — every expectation is recomputed in the test from observed state or source formulas, never read back from the double:

- descriptor contract (id/label/family, callable builder)
- scene assembly: glass shell + 7 blobs + 28-bubble points cloud; staged radius order; warmed crystal-glass shell override (`attenuationDistance` 2.5 vs kit default 3.0, amber attenuation colour) produced through the real `makeCrystalGlass` helper
- frame animation: shell-containment clamps (`|y| <= 0.85`, `hypot(x,z) <= 0.9 - radius/2`) held across sampled beats up to peak voice energy; swell band bounds; exact emissive heat mix `0.7 + energy*0.55 + respond*0.25`; respond-driven warmth shift with red-channel saturation clamp at 1 while blue stays fixed; bubble sine ride inside the 0.82 ring; exact opacity mix; fixed 0.0035 rad/frame shell yaw accumulation
- input-insensitivity to `listen`/`low`, and replay determinism of positions at a revisited instant
- dispose: all 9 geometries and all 9 materials disposed, parent emptied

## Evidence (test-only change)

- `bunx vitest run src/__tests__/stories-concepts-lava.test.ts` (in `packages/ui`): **Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 17 passed (17)** — re-run against current origin/develop base immediately before filing.
- `bunx biome check --write src/__tests__/stories-concepts-lava.test.ts`: clean ("Checked 1 file ... No fixes applied" after the initial format pass).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/ui`: the new test file appears nowhere in the output (checked by grep in two environments; remaining diagnostics are pre-existing and unrelated to this file).
- The diff touches only one new test file (+573/-0).

b3:Tef2,
## What

Adds `packages/agent/src/runtime/operations/index.test.ts` — unit coverage for the RuntimeOperation public-surface barrel (`packages/agent/src/runtime/operations/index.ts`), which had no same-named test file on `develop`.

## Why

The barrel is the documented import surface every consumer of runtime operations goes through, but nothing pinned it. A broken or accidentally shadowed re-export would surface only at consumer call sites. The sibling implementation modules (`classifier`, `cold-strategy`, `health`, `health-checks`, `manager`, `reload-hot`, `repository`, `vault-bridge`) each have their own suites; this closes the remaining gap at the barrel itself.

## What the suite covers (15 cases)

- **Namespace surface:** `Object.keys` of the barrel namespace equals exactly the 24 documented runtime exports — sibling-internal helpers (`describeError`, `VaultResolveError`, `resolveOptimizedPromptIntegrityKey`) stay out of the public surface.
- **Re-export identity:** every binding is the same reference as its sibling module's direct export (`toBe`) across all eight source modules — proves no rewrap/shadowing.
- **Live behavior through the barrel (real modules, no mocks):**
  - classifier tiers via the barrel: restart → cold, same-provider switch → hot, `env.` config-reload → hot, non-hot path → cold;
  - `defaultClassifier` parity with `classifyOperation`;
  - end-to-end cold restart through `createColdStrategy`: replacement runtime returned, restart reason forwarded, single succeeded `cold-restart` phase with timestamps;
  - vault-ref round trip (`formatVaultRef` / `isVaultRef` / `parseVaultRef`, malformed inputs) and `vaultKeyForProviderApiKey` canonical output plus its two `TypeError` branches;
  - `builtInHealthChecks` contains exactly the four exported checks in order, each asserted with observed name/required/timeoutMs metadata;
  - `new HealthChecker()` with an empty registry reports `{ passed: [], failed: [], ok: true }`.

## Evidence (test-only diff; touches only the new test file)

- `bunx vitest run packages/agent/src/runtime/operations/index.test.ts` → **Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 15 passed (15)** (re-fetched `develop` immediately before filing; base unchanged at `da1203a930100fbd5e51fa8100ca1819cb85d06d`, so these counts reproduce on current develop).
- `bunx biome check --write` applied once, then `bunx biome check <file>` → clean ("Checked 1 file ... No fixes applied").
- `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in `packages/agent` → the new file appears nowhere in the output (grep for `index.test.ts` exits 1).
- Diff is +266/-0, new file only. No production behavior changed.
- This is a fork PR: hosted CI does not run on it; the counts above are quoted from local runs of the real runner (`vitest`, which owns `packages/agent`'s unit lane).

## Summary

Adds `packages/core/src/testing/computer-use-conformance.test.ts`, a new colocated vitest suite for the interaction adapter conformance runner in `packages/core/src/testing/computer-use-conformance.ts` (which previously had no same-named suite anywhere in the repo). The diff is a single new test file: **+563/−0**, no production code touched.

The suite drives the real runner through a deterministic in-process `InteractionAdapter` (plain objects, no module mocks) and asserts observable behavior:

- `REQUIRED_INTERACTION_CONFORMANCE_CASES` exposes exactly the seven required case names in canonical order.
- Happy path: a truthful adapter passes all checks; report/checks/capabilities envelopes are frozen; check order is `capabilities`, `observation`, the seven cases, then `lease_contention` and `lease_expiry`.
- Fail-closed branches, each asserted by typed error code plus message/context detail:
  - mismatched adapter/session/surface identifiers;
  - stale surface generation at entry (`STALE_INTERACTION_REFERENCE`);
  - missing required fixture (names `'confirmation'`) and duplicate fixture names;
  - invalid capability/observation payloads wrapped as `INTERACTION_ADAPTER_CONFORMANCE_FAILED` with the original `INVALID_INTERACTION_CONTRACT` cause preserved;
  - capabilities advertising another adapter's identity;
  - unadvertised supplied surface kind;
  - non-executable session state (`INVALID_INTERACTION_CONTRACT`);
  - observation escaping the requested session surface;
  - unadvertised observation channels;
  - unsupported-case fixture built on an advertised action kind, and the inverse rule for non-unsupported fixtures;
  - stale-observation fixture with no observation binding;
  - wrong result status, asserting expected/actual status context.
- `runInteractionLeaseConformance()` returns frozen, deterministic, passed contention/expiry checks.

Two defensive branches in the runner ("Supplied conformance surface is not registered", stale surface inside a successful result observation) are unreachable through the public API because upstream contract validators reject those inputs first; no aspirational tests were written for them.

## Test evidence

- `bunx vitest run src/testing/computer-use-conformance.test.ts` (in `packages/core`, against current `origin/develop` @ `65d589387dac`): **1 file, 18 tests passed**.
- `bunx biome check src/testing/computer-use-conformance.test.ts`: clean, no fixes applied.
- Type checking: `packages/core/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/**/*.test.ts`, so the package-wide `tsc --noEmit` gate cannot see test files at all (the required grep for this filename in its output is empty). To produce real type evidence, the file was also checked directly with `tsc --noEmit` under the repository's root compiler options (`--strict --target es2022 --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler --lib es2023,dom,dom.iterable --allowImportingTsExtensions`): **clean, zero errors**. This single-file check caught and fixed three real type errors during development that neither vitest nor the package tsc gate would have surfaced.

This is a fork contribution: hosted CI does not run on this pull request. All counts above were executed locally against current `origin/develop` immediately before filing.

b7:Tf7a,
## What

Adds `packages/core/src/features/autonomy/index.test.ts` — a new unit suite for the features/autonomy entry barrel (`packages/core/src/features/autonomy/index.ts`). Test-only change: no production code is touched (single new file, +557/-0).

## Why

The barrel had no same-named test file anywhere on develop, yet it is load-bearing in two ways: consumers import autonomy through it, and its import-time `anchorBundleSafety("FEATURES_AUTONOMY_INDEX", ...)` side effect is what keeps its bindings alive in the on-device mobile bundle (the Bun.build re-export-barrel-drop workaround). Neither behavior was pinned by any existing suite; the sibling suites cover the leaves (action/providers/service), not the entry.

## Coverage

- Bundle-safety anchor: importing the entry registers the `__bundle_safety_FEATURES_AUTONOMY_INDEX__` global holding all ten re-exported bindings, each identity-equal (`toBe`) to a direct leaf-module import.
- Export surface: every documented export resolves to its leaf binding.
- Actions through the entry: ENABLE/DISABLE_AUTONOMOUS_MODE drive a real stateful fake service (loop toggled, live status mirrored into result data, callback fired once, turnComplete contract); the missing-service path returns the explicit `autonomy_service_unavailable` result and fails validation; the legacy `"autonomy"` service-name fallback still resolves; ESCALATE validation gates on service + autonomous room + configured admin; ESCALATE admin stores the escalation memory in the agent room and fires the callback; an `owner` target returns the explicit `unsupported_escalation_target` failure.
- Routes through the entry: GET /autonomy/status success payload (including the character-name fallback) and the 503 no-service path; POST /autonomy/toggle flips both directions; POST /autonomy/interval rejects missing, non-numeric, sub-5000 ms, and over-600000 ms values with 400 without mutating the service, and applies an in-range value.
- Providers through the entry: AUTONOMY_STATUS running state, the 24 h interval clamp, and explicit unavailability without the service; ADMIN_CHAT_HISTORY stays out of non-autonomous rooms.

Mocks stand in only for the `IAgentRuntime`/service collaborators; the actions, routes, and providers under test are the real implementations reached through the public entry.

b8:T3025,
## What

Adds a new unit suite for the liquid-metal voice-orb concept at
`packages/ui/stories/src/concepts/liquidmetal.ts`, which had no same-named test
file anywhere on `develop`. The diff is one new file,
`packages/ui/src/__tests__/stories-concepts-liquidmetal.test.ts` (+549/-0); no
production code is touched.

## Why

The concept module is pure runtime behaviour with zero coverage: it assembles a
chrome sphere through the injected `three/webgpu` + `three/tsl` surfaces, retunes
the orb-kit gem material into a smooth mirror, wires a fresnel rim light through
the live `uAccent`/`uRespond` uniforms, and deforms 1,617 vertices every frame.
The suite follows the established `stories-concepts-*` convention (see
`stories-concepts-lava.test.ts`) and drives the real module through hand-rolled
in-memory doubles whose calls are recorded; every expectation is recomputed in
the test, never read back from the subject.

## Coverage

- Descriptor contract: `id: "liquidmetal"`, `label: "liquid"`,
  `family: "abstract"`, callable builder.
- Scene assembly: exactly one sphere mesh on the parent at radius 0.95 with
  48x32 segments (1,617 vertices), material retuned from the
  `makeChromeGem` defaults (`flatShading: false`, `roughness: 0.03`,
  `metalness: 1`, `envMapIntensity: 1.8`, colour `(0.95, 0.97, 1.0)`).
- Rim light: lazy-evaluated TSL stand-ins prove the emissive graph re-prices
  live with `uRespond` (exact `(0.08 + 0.55*respond)/0.08` factor) and scales
  linearly with `uAccent`.
- Frame animation, all recomputed independently:
  - displacement stays purely radial for every vertex across beats
    (tangential residual < 1e-5);
  - amplitude envelope holds at the declared worst case
    `0.12 * (0.3 + 0.9 + 0.35)` while the blob still moves at idle;
  - idle wobble scales exactly linearly with energy (per-vertex ratio
    `(0.3+0.45)/0.3 = 2.5`);
  - crest sharpening activates only above the respond threshold and pushes
    crests beyond pure amplitude gain without ever flipping phase;
  - the threshold boundary itself: `respond = 0.01` still tracks pure
    amplitude scaling (strict `>` branch);
  - position attribute marked dirty + normals recomputed once per frame;
  - yaw drifts linearly (`0.08 * t`) while pitch rides its bounded sine;
  - `listen`/`low` inputs provably change nothing (byte-identical snapshot);
  - replaying the same instant reproduces byte-identical positions.
- Teardown: geometry + material disposed, mesh removed from the parent.

## What

Adds a new unit suite for `packages/ui/src/platform/remote-controller.ts` — the renderer adapter for the desktop remote-control identity — co-located as `packages/ui/src/platform/remote-controller.test.ts`. This is a **test-only** change: one new file, no production code touched (+548/-0 against `develop`).

The suite drives the real module through its real dependency seam: a recording fake `ElectrobunRendererRpc` installed at `window.__ELIZA_ELECTROBUN_RPC__` (the same injection point the Electrobun main process uses), so every assertion exercises the actual adapter code path over the actual bridge helper (`invokeDesktopBridgeRequest`) rather than mocking the module under test.

## Coverage

18 cases across all six exported functions:

- **`getOrCreateRemoteControllerIdentity`** — exact RPC routing (`remoteControllerGetOrCreateIdentity`) and params; platform-derived display-name defaults for macOS (`MacIntel` → "My Mac"), Windows (`Win32` → "My Windows PC"), and Linux (`Linux x86_64` → "My Linux computer"); explicit `displayName` winning over the platform default; fail-closed rejection when the bridge returns no identity.
- **`createRemoteCommand`** — flattening of controller/target identities into `controllerDeviceId` / `controllerKeyId` / `targetRuntimeId` / `targetKeyId` / `targetEncryptionPublicKeyJwk`; passthrough of the signed result including the `recoveredPending` recovery flag in both states; rejection when signing is unavailable.
- **`acknowledgeRemoteCommandEnqueue`** — input forwarded verbatim as request params; `acknowledged` unwrapping for both `true` and `false`; rejection when the acknowledgement channel is unavailable.
- **`openRemoteCommandResult`** — envelope/command/target identity forwarded verbatim; decrypted result passthrough; rejection when decryption is unavailable.
- **`openRemoteCommandStartReceipt`** — start-receipt field passthrough; rejection when verification is unavailable.
- **`clearRemoteControllerSessionState`** — resolves `true` on success, resolves `false` without throwing when the main process reports `cleared: false`, and resolves `false` when the desktop bridge is absent entirely (no throw — distinct from the other operations).

Each of the five distinct fail-closed error messages is asserted verbatim.

A same-named suite already exists on develop (`__tests__/facts-and-relationships.test.ts`, landed via #25721), so this pull request is **strictly additive**: 17 new cases appended in new `describe` blocks, **+476/-0**, no existing line touched, no case rewritten or removed.

## New coverage (all driving the real module, no mock-asserts-mock)

**`parseFactsAndRelationshipsOutput` branches not previously pinned**
- prose containing no JSON object rejects with `FACTS_MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` (the tolerant parser finds nothing to salvage)
- non-array `facts`, non-array `relationships`, and non-string `thought` each reject with `FACTS_MODEL_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID`
- a malformed fact entry (number at index) throws with `context: { factIndex: 1 }`
- blank fact strings are dropped after trimming; missing subject defaults to `"user"`; padded relationship fields are trimmed

**Exported tool contract**
- `createFactsAndRelationshipsTool()` returns a strict function tool whose name matches `FACTS_AND_RELATIONSHIPS_TOOL_NAME` and whose `parameters` is the shared `factsAndRelationshipsSchema`

**Stage behavior (`runFactsAndRelationshipsStage`)**
- duplicate candidates collapse before the model call: case/punctuation-duplicate facts yield exactly one `- fact:` line; cross-case duplicate relationship pairs (`Works With!` vs `works_with`) dedupe after snake_case predicate normalization, observed in the prompt block, persisted echo content, and `createRelationship` tags
- self-relationship (`user mentors user`) writes the echo memory but never creates a source===target entity edge
- `getMemories` rejection degrades to no-dedup and reports under scope `FactsAndRelationships.searchSimilarFacts`; `getRelationships` rejection reports under `FactsAndRelationships.fetchExistingRelationships`; both proceed without the corresponding prompt block
- non-array facts-store response is tolerated silently (treated as no known facts, no `reportError`)
- fact subjects resolve at persistence time to the agent (`Eliza` character name) or directly via UUID subject
- secret-shaped but short tokens are redacted before the model sees them and stay redacted at persistence, without dropping the fact
- `ELIZA_PLATFORM=ios` short-circuits the whole stage ("skipped on mobile"): no model call, no writes

# Risks

Moderate. This changes the Telegram delivery ledger namespace and canonical message identity from account-independent epoch 1 state to bot-account-scoped epoch 2 state. A bad boundary could suppress another bot's event or duplicate a reply.

Mitigations:

- the immutable numeric bot ID survives secret rotation;
- opaque credentials use a SHA-256 account fingerprint and are never serialized raw;
- the Durable Object name, canonical message ID, reminders, receipts, and gateway reconciliation all use the same account scope;
- canonical receiver IDs are bounded to 160 characters with a deterministic hash fallback;
- old gateway binaries may still write epoch 1 state during a rolling deployment, but epoch 2 never imports an ambiguous epoch 1 tombstone;
- epoch 1 state expires after the existing 30-day delivery TTL.

No migration, staging deploy, production deploy, or feature-flag change is included.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

The original patch derived and forwarded `connectorAccountId`, but Telegram `update_id` is bot-scoped while the delivery ledger was still keyed only by project, sender, and update. Two bots could therefore collide in one Durable Object and replay or fence each other's delivery.

This revision closes that boundary:

- numeric bot-token prefixes map to stable `bot:<bot-id>` identities across secret rotation;
- opaque tokens map to `bot:<sha256(token)>` without disclosing the credential;
- epoch 2 Durable Objects are keyed by project, connector account, and sender;
- canonical message IDs include the connector account and fall back to a bounded hash when needed;
- reminders and stored provider receipts use the same scope;
- gateway reconciliation sends `deliveryEpoch: 2` and `connectorAccountId`;
- the authenticated `/delivery` receiver validates epoch, account, sender, and message before allocating state;
- account-independent epoch 1 requests remain isolated only for rolling compatibility.

Code provenance: this aligns the Telegram edge producer with the existing gateway identity contract and receiver validation, building on work by @NubsCarson, @lalalune, and @0xSolace.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix with an internal delivery-ledger epoch boundary.

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing documentation change is needed. The epoch behavior and quarantine rationale are documented next to the internal delivery contract.

**What the suite pins (22 cases, real hooks + pure function, only the network boundary and Steward session are mocked):**

- `formatApprovalTimestamp`: null / empty / unparseable inputs return null; a parseable UTC timestamp formats to the observed `en-US` label under the package's pinned `TZ=UTC`.
- `useApprovalRequests`: unwraps `approvalRequests`; unfiltered calls hit the bare endpoint; `{ status }` appends the query string; signed-out sessions stay idle and never call the API.
- `useApproveRequest` / `useDenyRequest`: POST path percent-encodes ids (`req/7` -> `req%2F7`); deny sends the caller's reason verbatim and falls back to `"denied by owner"` when omitted.
- `useBallots`: status-filtered fetch and `ballots` unwrap.
- `useVoteBallot`: success resolves the recorded outcome; failure rejects with the server error text, falling back to `"Unable to record vote."` when absent.
- `useTallyBallot` / `useCancelBallot` / `useCancelSensitiveRequest`: empty-JSON POST bodies, response passthrough, and the always-present `reason` field.
- `useSensitiveRequest`: null and whitespace-only ids stay disabled with zero API calls; ids are trimmed before the detail request; both `{ request }` envelope and plain payloads normalize correctly.

Test-only change: no production file is modified; the diff is one new file, +536/-0.

## What

Adds `packages/core/src/features/advanced-memory/evaluators/memory-items.test.ts` — a new, self-contained vitest suite for the long-term-memory evaluator (`longTermMemoryEvaluator`) and the `memoryItems` registry export in `packages/core/src/features/advanced-memory/evaluators/memory-items.ts`. **Test-only diff: one new file, +535/-0. No production code changes.**

## Why

The module had no same-named test suite on `develop`; only the comparator hook was covered (by `memory-items.safe-sort.test.ts`, which this suite deliberately does not duplicate). Everything else the evaluator decides at runtime — gating, context assembly, prompt rendering, model-output parsing, and storage policy — was untested.

## What is covered

- `shouldRun`: rejects incomplete messages before touching any service; returns false with no MemoryService registered; skips the agent's own messages even when extraction is enabled; short-circuits on a disabled config before counting messages; delegates to `shouldRunExtraction` with the live room message count in both directions.
- `prepare`: throws when no MemoryService is registered; filters synthetic conversation artifacts and orders genuine turns oldest-first; formats existing memories as `[category] content (confidence: N)` with the `None yet` fallback; floors the recent-messages fetch limit at 1.
- `prompt`: renders each speaker through the real fallback chain (agent character name → `senderName` → entity id) and the `[non-text message]` placeholder; embeds the existing-memory block verbatim between its labelled sections.
- `parse`: rejects malformed envelopes (null, scalar, array, missing memories array); normalizes valid entries (trims content, lowercases categories); drops unknown-category, blank-content, and non-numeric-confidence entries while keeping valid siblings; treats an explicit empty array as an empty successful output.
- `storeLongTermMemory` processor: applies the `max(longTermConfidenceThreshold, 0.85)` confidence floor in both regimes; counts only stored extractions in the result values; still advances the extraction checkpoint when nothing qualifies.

Every assertion drives the real exported evaluator object through its public lifecycle methods against a typed mock runtime (`createMockRuntime`) and a recording MemoryService double — no mock returns are asserted against themselves.

- animation: rotations follow time and energy (body y=t*0.04, wobble x, cracks mirror, core counter-rotates, sparks orbit speed scales with energy); sustained energy clamps totalHeat at 1.0 and every heat-driven output pins at its ceiling
- respond flare state machine: strictly-greater-than-0.7 trigger (respond=0.7 exactly never fires), single-frame spike, linear decay back to the bit-exact idle baseline, and the `flareDecay < 0.1` hysteresis producing a sawtooth re-arm under sustained responding
- dispose releases all six geometries/materials plus the particles' own resources and empties the parent

Placement note: the suite lives in `packages/ui/src/__tests__/` rather than beside the source because the package vitest lane collects only `src/**`, `__tests__/**`, and `test/**`, and the package tsconfig includes only `src` — a suite inside `stories/src/` would never be collected by CI nor typechecked.

## What

The module had no same-named test anywhere on `develop`.

## Coverage

Real behaviour of the real module — no mocks standing in for the subject:

- **`parseMapsCardBody`** — all five card kinds (`place`, `places`, `route`, `handoff`, `locate`) parsed end-to-end from JSON fixtures, plus rejection paths: malformed JSON, non-object payloads, unknown kinds; coordinate range boundaries (±90/±180 inclusive pass, beyond fails); string-length bounds (300-char name passes, 301 rejected); category filtering order (invalid entries dropped *before* the 8-cap); the `MAX_MAPS_CARD_PLACES` overflow rule (12 entries keep the first 10; trailing garbage after a full page is never parsed, garbage below the cap rejects the card); over-long optional fields degrading to `null` rather than rejecting (`attribution`, `nextCursor`); absent/empty `formattedAddress`/`sharedAt` omitting their keys entirely; route travel-mode allowlisting and metric bounds; handoff URI policy enforcement; locate intent validation.
- **`isAllowedMapsUri`** — `geo:` scheme requires a leading coordinate digit (negative coordinates pass, `+`-prefixed and non-numeric fail); https-only links restricted to `maps.apple.com` and `www.openstreetmap.org`; lookalike hosts, wrong schemes, and unparseable strings rejected.
- **`findMapsCardRegions`** — exact fence-to-fence offset contract (`text.slice(start, end)` reproduces the full block including fences); multiple cards collected in order with malformed blocks skipped mid-scan; padded fences and CRLF tolerated; no-card text returns `[]`; repeated calls do not leak global-regex `lastIndex` state between invocations.

## What

Adds a new unit suite for `packages/ui/stories/src/concepts/aurora.ts`, the aurora voice-orb concept (five curved translucent ribbons plus a drifting star cloud), which previously had no test coverage anywhere on develop.

**Placement note:** `stories/` has no test runner of its own (no package.json, and the package vitest lane collects only `src/**/*.test.*`), so the suite lives at `packages/ui/src/__tests__/stories-concepts-aurora.test.ts`, where the owning package's existing unit lane collects and typechecks it. The subject is imported directly from its canonical location.

## How it tests

The suite drives the **real** module through the same seam production uses: `concept.build(THREE, TSL, U, parent)` receives its three.js surface as an injected parameter (`WebGPUModule = Record<string, any>` per orb-kit), so a recording double supplies that boundary while every expectation is recomputed independently in the test — nothing is asserted by reading a mock's own output back.

Covered behaviour:

- **Descriptor contract** — id/label/family registration, callable builder.
- **Ribbon geometry bend** — five PlaneGeometries bent onto a cylindrical arc: equator vertices keep their flat positions, every off-equator vertex gains negative depth (backward wrap), ribbon ends flare past the flat plane width, the height grid stays symmetric about the equator, normals are computed.
- **Material contract** — each ribbon is a translucent, non-depth-writing, double-sided normal-blended curtain at opacity 0.45; base hues are pairwise distinct within unit range (per-ribbon hue preservation).
- **Star cloud** — exactly 60 points inside the documented r∈[0.5, 1.25] shell, small cool translucent points, frustum culling disabled.
- **Frame animation** — idle floor opacities (0.42 ribbons / 0.5 stars), response-curve brightening recomputed from captured bases with channels saturating at exactly 1, opacity clamping at the 0.7 ceiling, five pairwise-distinct headings while swaying, pitch/position envelope bounds across sampled times, fixed star drift rates, insensitivity to `listen`/`low` inputs, and whole-state determinism when a frame replays.
- **Dispose** — every geometry and material disposed, all six added children detached from the parent group.

No `expectTypeOf`, no `vi.mock` of the subject, no type-only assertions.

# Evidence Details

## Real LLM-call trajectory

For agent/action/provider/prompt/model changes, use a real live-model run, not
the deterministic proxy. Produce with:

```bash
  packages/scenario-runner/bin/eliza-scenarios run <scenario> --report <out.json>
```

Link the JSON report, run viewer, native jsonl, or write `N/A - <reason>`.

## Backend + frontend logs

Backend: structured logger lines ([ClassName] …) showing the code path firing end to end.
Frontend: console + network trace showing the request/response and state change.
Paste here inline (wrap long output in a `<details>` block), or write
`N/A - <reason>`.

## Screenshots (before / after) + video walkthrough

Full-page before AND after screenshots are required for any UI change. Include a
video click-through of the flow.

```bash
  bun run evidence:doctor                 (check capture tools; prints fixes for any missing)
  bun run test:e2e:record                 (general E2E recordings)
  bun run test:matrix:review              (capture into one verified evidence bundle)
  bun run evidence:review:no-open -- --bundle=evidence/runs/<run-id>
                                          (re-open the exact matrix run)
  bun run --cwd packages/app audit:app    (app + cloud UI — REQUIRED for UI changes)
```

The matrix command creates and verifies one named bundle, then passes that
exact run to the reviewer. Do not replace the `--bundle` path with raw producer
directories; `--source` is only for explicit archived/ad-hoc compatibility.

A UI-touching diff (rendered `.tsx`/`.css`/`.svg` under `packages/app`,
`packages/ui`, `apps/app`, …) MUST attach real screenshot/video/OCR artifacts —
the CI evidence gate rejects `N/A` on those rows for such diffs, label or not.
If a capture tool is missing, `evidence:doctor` prints the install command;
install it rather than marking evidence `N/A`.

## What

Adds `packages/core/src/sessions/index.test.ts` — a new vitest suite for the public sessions barrel (`packages/core/src/sessions/index.ts`), which had no same-named test file anywhere on current `develop`. Test-only diff: one new file, no deletions, no production changes.

The barrel re-exports three modules (`session-key.ts`, `types.ts`, `provider.ts`); every test drives the real modules through that barrel with no mocks:

- exported default constants (`DEFAULT_AGENT_ID`, `DEFAULT_MAIN_KEY`, `DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID`, reset triggers, idle window)
- subagent key build→parse round-trip plus ACP/subagent discriminator flags
- DM peer-key `dmScope` matrix (main fallback, per-peer, per-channel-peer, per-account-channel-peer) and non-DM group/channel peer keys
- group history keys
- request↔store session key conversions, including agent-prefixed passthrough and malformed-input behavior
- agent resolution from session keys and thread-scoped key resolution (`useSuffix`, parent echo)
- entry lifecycle: `createSessionEntry` defaults vs overrides; `mergeSessionEntry` new/existing merges, identity preservation and explicit rekeying, and the `updatedAt = max(existing, patch, now)` rule including future timestamps and never-lowering guarantees
- `isValidSessionEntry` accept/reject matrix (nullish, primitives, arrays, empty id, wrong types)
- `extractSessionContext` precedence chain: direct memory props > metadata fields > stored session entry, and `null` when no session info exists
- provider behavior through real `get()` calls: full ordered session-context rendering including the deny warning line, skills snapshot listing, send-policy deny/allow paths, default/custom names, provider position, and `getSessionProviders` ordering

## Why

Sibling coverage existed only for `session-key.ts`; the barrel's type and provider surfaces were untested. This adds behavior-preserving, test-only value on top of current develop.

## Verification

- `bunx vitest run src/sessions/index.test.ts` in `packages/core`: **1 test file passed, 25/25 tests passed** against current develop sources (the four sessions modules are byte-identical between branch base `f11cedd35e5a` and develop `16c9edf96222`).
- `bunx biome check src/sessions/index.test.ts`: clean, no diagnostics.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/core`: exit 0, zero errors; the new file appears nowhere in the output.
- Diff is additive-only: `git status` shows exactly one new test file for this branch; no existing suite was rewritten or deleted.

Note: this pull request comes from a fork, so hosted CI does not run on it — the counts above are real local runs quoted here.

## Summary

Extends the existing `packages/ui/src/components/shell/__tests__/useShellController.test.tsx` suite with 20 new cases covering branches it did not previously reach. Strictly additive: **+496/-0 on one test file**; no production code, no existing cases rewritten or removed.

## What is covered

- **omi pendant relay** (`PENDANT_VOICE_TRANSCRIPT_EVENT`): a finalized pendant transcript routes as a `VOICE_DM` turn with the `pendant:<segmentId>` dedupe id and full provenance metadata; the id is omitted when the segment has none; a blank transcript is ignored.
- **VISION capture**: the tap sends the screen-vision intent turn (`metadata.vision.surface = "screen"`), `visionCapturing` pulses until the reply is in flight, and a stopped agent neither sends nor pulses (`canSend` false).
- **send() edge guards**: whitespace-only text without attachments is a no-op; an image-only send with empty text goes through and does not set the voice-originated latch; options (`channelType`, `metadata`, `clientMessageId`) are forwarded verbatim.
- **capture-failure copy + once-per-grant-epoch latch**: unknown failures use the generic "Could not start the microphone" wording; a post-capture cloud-STT error surfaces the "Didn't catch that" transcription wording (not a microphone accusation); a repeated failure while unresolved does not re-toast, one successful open re-arms the notice for a later denial.
- **Silent-drop hint**: the factory's `onSilentDrop` fires the short info notice ("Didn't catch that — try again.").
- **Interim transcript + cancelRecording (#20483)**: a non-final segment shows as live transcript; cancel disposes without the stop() drain, clearing recording/transcript.
- **stop() routing**: halts a streaming turn via `handleChatStop`; during pure TTS playback it stops speech but must not tear down the chat stream.
- **Agent voice mute projection**: the controller projects voice-output's mute state and delegates the toggle.
- **unlockAudio routing**: realtime-owned sessions unlock through the realtime client; idle realtime falls back to voice output.
- **voice-settings apply validation**: an unrecognized `continuous` value is ignored entirely (no persistence, no engagement).
- **bootProgressSignal (#14040)**: present and advancing on fresh warming observations, `undefined` once ready.

## Verification (fork contributor — hosted CI does not run on this PR)

- `bunx vitest run src/components/shell/__tests__/useShellController.test.tsx` → **115 passed / 115** (95 pre-existing + 20 new), re-run immediately before filing against current `origin/develop`.
- `bunx biome check --write <file>` clean (subsequent read-only check: "No fixes applied").
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/ui`: the new test file appears nowhere in output (zero type errors introduced).
- Diff touches only `packages/ui/src/components/shell/__tests__/useShellController.test.tsx` (+496/-0).

## Summary

Extends unit coverage for `packages/core/src/runtime/system-prompt.ts` additively: +301/-0 in `packages/core/src/runtime/__tests__/system-prompt.test.ts`, no production code touched.

The existing suite covered `buildCanonicalSystemPrompt`, `resolveEffectiveSystemPrompt`, `dropDuplicateLeadingSystemMessage`, and `buildCharacterStyleDirections` happy paths. This change adds cases for the previously untested exports and uncovered branches:

- `renderSystemPromptBio`: string trim; array join with trimming/dropping of empty and non-string entries; non-string/non-array inputs return `""`.
- `normalizeSystemPromptRole`: trim + uppercase; blank/missing roles map to `undefined`.
- `buildCanonicalSystemPrompt`: blank name falls back to "the agent" with token substitution; no character/role renders empty; blank role omits the role line; bio-only prompt renders under the About heading.
- `textFromChatMessageContent`: string trim; non-string/non-array returns `""`; array parts join trimmed text with newlines while malformed parts (nulls, arrays, non-object, non-string `text`) are skipped.
- `extractLeadingSystemPrompt`: absent/empty/system-less lists return `undefined`; multi-part system content joins; whitespace-only leading system message is treated as absent.
- `resolveEffectiveSystemPrompt`: non-object params fall through to fallback; explicit non-string `params.system` short-circuits to `undefined` without consulting messages/fallback; explicitly present but textless `params.system` preserves `""`; textless leading message falls through to a trimmed fallback; blank/non-string fallback maps to `undefined`.
- `dropDuplicateLeadingSystemMessage`: undefined/empty pass-through; unchanged output when there is no resolved prompt; trimmed comparison drops padded duplicates; structured content parts match too.
- `renderChatMessagesForPrompt` (previously untested): role-headed blocks joined by blank lines; textless messages skipped; `omitDuplicateSystem` removes only the first matching leading system message (trimmed compare); blank omit value is inert; omit applies only at index 0 with role `system`; all-skipped renders `undefined`.

All expectations record observed behavior of the current module; every case drives the real functions directly — no mocks, no type-level assertions.

## Evidence

- Base: origin/develop @ `e3e63588fd59` (suite re-fetched and re-run immediately before filing; neither the source nor the existing suite changed between the session's first fetch and this base).
- `bunx vitest run src/runtime/__tests__/system-prompt.test.ts` (packages/core): **Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 43 passed (43)** — 10 pre-existing + 33 new.
- `bunx biome check --write packages/core/src/runtime/__tests__/system-prompt.test.ts`: clean (formatting applied to the new lines only; config verified present, checkout not sparse).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` in packages/core: completed with no output; grep for `system-prompt.test` over the full log matched nothing.
- Diff scope: single test file, `+301/-0` versus base (`git diff --numstat origin/develop..HEAD` = `301 0`). No line of the existing suite was modified or deleted.

This PR comes from a fork, so hosted CI does not run on it — the checks above are local runs whose exact counts are quoted here.

c9:T2dec,
## What

Adds `packages/shared/src/api/http-helpers.test.ts` — a new, additive-only suite (+492/−0, no other files touched) covering the runtime surface re-exported by `packages/shared/src/api/http-helpers.ts`: `DEFAULT_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, `readRequestBodyBuffer`, `readRequestBody`, `readJsonBody`, `sendJson`, and `sendJsonError`.

Every case drives the real exported helpers against a live `node:http` exchange on loopback — no mocks of the module under test. The covered behavior:

- **Bounded body reads** — chunk concatenation; repeat readers receive the SAME memoized buffer (`Symbol.for` cache) without re-consuming the stream; empty bodies; explicit `encoding` handling (utf-8/base64).
- **Size guards** — default cap rejects oversized bodies with typed `HTTP_REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE` carrying `{maxBytes, observedBytes}` context; custom `tooLargeMessage`; `returnNullOnTooLarge` / `destroyOnTooLarge` combinations including stream destruction; the guard re-applied to an already-memoized buffer on repeat reads.
- **`readJsonBody`** — object parsing memoized on the request (`req.body` exposed, second call served from cache); non-object rejection by default (arrays/scalars/null) with 400 JSON error envelope; `requireObject: false` accepts arrays and scalars; dedicated parse-error vs non-object statuses/messages, all overridable; read failures (including size overflow) translated to the configured read-error response (default 413).
- **Safe responders** — `sendJson` / `sendJsonError` status defaults and overrides, `application/json` content type, `{error}` envelope, and no synchronous throw when the client vanished before the write.

Note: an existing suite covers core's own `packages/core/src/api/http-helpers.ts` implementation directly; this PR covers the shared re-export surface that shared-package consumers actually import.

## Evidence

Test-only change; no production behavior modified.

- `bunx vitest run packages/shared/src/api/http-helpers.test.ts` → **Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 19 passed (19)** (also green via the package lane `node ../scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ./vitest.config.ts src/api/http-helpers.test.ts`).
- `bunx @biomejs/biome check src/api/http-helpers.test.ts` → clean, no fixes needed.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in `packages/shared` → the new test file appears nowhere in the output.

Adds a first unit suite for `packages/ui/src/state/autonomy.ts` (client-side
autonomy run-health tracking: sequence-gap detection over streamed event
envelopes, recovery, reconnect hydration from the carried store, dedup,
ledger trimming, watermark cursor semantics, and gap-replay request
building). No production code is touched; the diff is one new co-located
vitest file (+490/−0) matching the sibling `*.test.ts` convention already
used throughout `packages/ui/src/state/`.

## Evidence

- `bunx vitest run packages/ui/src/state/autonomy.test.ts` → **Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 21 passed (21)** against current `origin/develop` (`de774b8757`). Re-fetched immediately before filing; `origin/develop` had not moved since the branch point.
- `bunx biome check packages/ui/src/state/autonomy.test.ts` → clean ("Checked 1 file … No fixes applied"). Verified non-vacuous: `biome.json` exists at the repo root and the checkout is not sparse.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit -p .` in `packages/ui`: `autonomy.test.ts` appears **nowhere** in the output. The run reports 8 pre-existing errors in files this diff does not touch (`packages/core/src/cloud-routing.ts`, `src/cloud/mcps/lib/use-mcps.test.tsx`, `src/cloud/organization/data/use-credentials.test.tsx`).
- The diff touches only `packages/ui/src/state/autonomy.test.ts`. Every case drives the real module — no mocks, no `expectTypeOf`.

## Note for reviewers

While writing the suite I observed behavior that looks like a latent bug rather than intended contract, so I did **not** assert it as expected: an incoming envelope whose `runId` is literally `"__proto__"` or `"constructor"` makes `mergeAutonomyEvents` throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')`, because `ensureRunHealth` reads the inherited property as a pre-existing truthy health object. This test-only diff covers the non-crashing guard branches instead (`constructor`/`prototype` runIds never enter `runIndex`); a production fix belongs in a separate, justified change.

## What the suite covers

- `mergeAutonomyEvents`: cold-start empty result; first-batch insertion with `lastSeq` and no invented gaps; gap detection metadata (`missingSeqs`, `gapCount`, `lastGapAt`, `runsWithNewGaps`); same-batch recovery (`recoveredAt`, `runsRecovered`); multi-gap partial fill across calls carrying the returned store forward; reconnect hydration from a carried store into a fresh health map; caller-input immutability (store and health map are cloned); duplicate counting by `eventId` and by the `runId:seq:stream` fallback key; envelopes without `runId`/`seq` stored but exempt from health tracking; prototype-dangerous runIds excluded from `runIndex`; `replay: true` marking unresolved runs `partial`; `maxEvents` trimming evicting seqs from `runIndex` with consistent rehydration; watermark cursor not moving backwards on late low-seq arrivals; non-ordinal `eventId` takeover of the cursor; fractional `seq` truncation onto the integer index.
- `buildAutonomyGapReplayRequests`: no requests without health; already-replayed seqs filtered out; requests sorted by `fromSeq`.
- `hasPendingAutonomyGaps`: false for empty/healthy maps, true when any run still misses seqs.
- `markPendingAutonomyGapsPartial`: only gapped runs become `partial`; explicit timestamp honored; default timestamp is now; deep-clone semantics with the input left untouched.

## CI note

This PR comes from a fork, so hosted CI does not run on it; all checks above were executed locally against the pushed head and their real outputs are quoted here.

Adds a real vitest unit suite for packages/ui/src/genui/validator.ts, which had no same-named test file on develop. The module's hostile-walk ceilings are covered by validator.unbounded.test.ts and its randomized never-throws contract by validator.fuzz.test.ts; this suite pins the structural spec-validation contract those specialized suites do not:

- accepted specs: minimal connected spec, snapshot prototypes severed, -0 normalized to +0, every frozen-catalog component name accepted, child refs honored across all binding slots (child, children, entryPointChild, contentChild, tabItems[].child)
- header validation: version/a2uiVersion rules, blank root, non-object specs
- components array: default 200-component cap boundary (200 ok, 201 rejected), maxComponents override, non-array rejection
- component records: missing/whitespace ids, duplicate ids, blank names, unknown catalog names
- image-source safety matrix: path-relative, data:image/, http(s)/blob accepted; javascript:, ftp:, data:text/html rejected as unsafe_url
- action allow-list: prefix matches accepted, unknown names rejected with the componentId-based path, malformed action shapes rejected, allowedActionNames exact-name admission, allowedActionPrefixes replacing (not unioning) the defaults
- reference integrity: dangling root, per-child missing_child reporting, multi-issue accumulation order
- hostile payloads: cyclic data, undefined/NaN/Infinity/function/symbol/bigint values, unsafe_field flagging for script-bearing keys, symbol-keyed and non-enumerable properties skipped silently
- size options: lowered maxJsonBytes override
- assertValidElizaGenUiSpec: passthrough on success and an Error whose message joins every issue message with newlines

All assertions record observed behavior of the real module driven end to end (no mocks); two initially aspirational expectations (index-based action paths, single-error counts where reference checks accumulate) were corrected to what the code actually does before landing.
